property_summary: If SetMinSum has never been called (or was called with the default zero), then after any Collect, MinSum must still be zero because the original SetMinSum sets it to _val while the buggy version leaves it as zero. The rule: when _am is zero, Collect should revert if MinSum is zero (since balance >= 0 and _am >= 0 but MinSum > 0 fails). Actually, the correct invariant is: if MinSum is 0 (i.e., SetMinSum never called), then Collect should succeed only when balance >=0 and balance >= _am and timestamp > unlockTime; but MinSum=0 always satisfies balance>=MinSum. So the difference is that the original SetMinSum can set MinSum to a non-zero value, while the buggy version always leaves it zero. Thus the property: For any valid _am, if SetMinSum was never called, Collect behaves the same regardless. Wait — the bug is that SetMinSum does nothing, so MinSum stays 0. The reference can set MinSum to a non-zero value after Initialized, but if Initialized is never called, both are same. The failing test should capture that MinSum remains 0 after any sequence. Simpler: After calling SetMinSum with some _val, if Initialized is called, then MinSum in reference is _val, in mutant it's 0. So call SetMinSum(x), then Initialized, then Collect(0). The reference contract's MinSum is x != 0, mutant's is 0. For Collect(0) to succeed, need balance >= MinSum. If balance >0 and unlockTime past, Collect in reference will revert because balance(>0) < MinSum(x>0)? Actually balance >= MinSum: if balance is small, might fail. Too complex. I propose: After SetMinSum is called with a non-zero value and Initialized called, the MinSum remains the set value in reference and zero in mutant. So we can check that after such calls, c.MinSum() != 0 in reference but 0 in mutant. So property: after SetMinSum(42) and Initialized, c.MinSum() == 42. The buggy version will have c.MinSum() == 0, which is different. So we fuzz over _val and ensure it's non-zero, and after the calls, assertTrue(c.MinSum() == _val). That will pass on reference and fail on mutant. However the test must work for all inputs: need _val != 0. Use vm.assume(_val != 0). Then drive calls: c.SetMinSum(_val); c.Initialized(); assertTrue(c.MinSum() == _val). That's it.
